text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Denmark will grant Vietnam $48 million for four water supply and sanitation projects which will be implemented over the next five years.

-- The departing Resident Representative of the United Nations Development Programme, Roy Morey, has urged Vietnamese Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet to continue macro-economic restructuring and improvements to the country's foreign investment environment.
-- A senior police lieutenant colonel and two captains have been arrested for alleged involvement in a drug trafficking case. Thirty people have been arrested in the probe so far.
-- The National Assembly's Standing Committee has called for prompt and strict trials for corruption cases which have been uncovered.
-- A Cuban Communist Party delegation held talks with the Secretary of Hanoi's Party Committee during a five-day visit to Vietnam.

-- Commander-in-chief James Nier of the U.S Veterans of Foreign War handed over documents and maps relating to the remains of Vietnamese soldiers missing in action (MIA) to the Chairman of the Vietnam Veteran Association Lieutenant General Tran Van Quang.
